description: Bank peer groupings for cross-bank calibration comparison

cohorts.name: European Tier 1 Investment Banks
cohorts.description: Major European G-SIBs with significant derivatives operations

calibration_expectations.rationale: EMIR Refit creates similar forcing function for all
CFTC Rewrite and ISDA proximity create similar pressures

cohorts.name: Japanese Megabanks
cohorts.description: Major Japanese banks subject to JSCC requirements

calibration_expectations.rationale: JSCC CDM mandate creates strong homogeneity expectation
Swiss banks traditionally less transparent about technology adoption

cohorts.name: Known CDM Production Users
cohorts.description: Banks with confirmed CDM production usage (per anchor-points.json)

calibration_expectations.rationale: Anchor points - these must be classified as ARCHITECT

network_adoption_thresholds.description: Thresholds for network effect pressure calculation (Enhancement 4)

tipping_point.description: When 40% of cohort adopts, remaining banks face intense pressure
tipping_point.rationale: Based on network effect research - adoption accelerates above this point

critical_mass.description: When 60% of cohort adopts, non-adopters face very high pressure

MEDIUM.description: Some adopters - moderate peer pressure emerging

HIGH.description: Above tipping point - significant peer pressure

CRITICAL.description: Critical mass reached - very high pressure to conform

usage_notes: Cohorts are used for peer calibration in consistency checking
A bank can belong to multiple cohorts
Known producers cohort provides hard constraints (must be ARCHITECT)
Other cohorts provide soft constraints (statistical consistency)
